medicines.uses: Relief of mild-to-moderate pain (headache, toothache, muscle ache) and fever reduction.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Hepatotoxicity (liver damage) with acute overdose; severe cutaneous adverse reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome).
medicines.storageInstructions: Store below 30°C in a dry place away from direct sunlight.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Can be taken with or without food.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Generally considered safe at recommended therapeutic doses under medical supervision; low clinical risk.
medicines.childrenWarning: Use child-specific pediatric liquid or suppository formulations with weight-based dosing.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Generally safe; monitor total daily dosage in patients with hepatic impairment.

medicines.uses: Treatment of bacterial infections including respiratory tract infections, otitis media, sinusitis, skin and urinary tract infections.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, oral candidiasis.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis), Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea, cholestatic jaundice, hepatitis.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store tablets below 25°C in a dry place. Refrigerate reconstituted oral suspension (2°C–8°C) and use within 7–10 days.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Take at the start of a meal to enhance absorption and reduce gastrointestinal upset.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and prescribed by a physician; low risk established in human studies.
medicines.childrenWarning: Dosage calculated strictly based on body weight using oral suspension.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Monitor renal function; dosage adjustment required in severe renal impairment.
medicines.maxDailyDose: 2000mg Amoxicillin component per day as directed by physician.

medicines.uses: Relief of mild-to-moderate pain, dysmenorrhea, dental pain, fever, rheumatoid arthritis, and osteoarthritis.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Heartburn, dyspepsia, nausea, abdominal discomfort, dizziness.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding, cardiovascular thrombotic risks, acute kidney injury.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store below 25°C in a cool, dry place.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Take with or after food or milk to minimize stomach irritation.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Contraindicated in third trimester due to risk of premature closure of ductus arteriosus and oligohydramnios.
medicines.childrenWarning: Use pediatric suspension; not recommended under 3 months or <5kg without medical advice.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Higher risk of serious GI bleeding and renal complications; use lowest effective dose.
medicines.maxDailyDose: 2400mg per 24 hours under medical supervision (1200mg OTC limit).

medicines.uses: Fast-acting relief of acute pain and inflammation in conditions like dysmenorrhea, migraine, post-traumatic pain, and dental pain.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Epigastric pain, nausea, diarrhea, abdominal cramps, headache.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Serious GI bleeding/ulceration, elevated liver enzymes, myocardial infarction risk, acute kidney injury.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store below 30°C in original package to protect from moisture and light.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Take before meals or on an empty stomach with fluid for rapid pain relief.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Contraindicated in third trimester; avoid during earlier pregnancy unless explicitly prescribed by a physician.
medicines.childrenWarning: Not recommended for children under 14 years of age.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Use lowest effective dose due to elevated GI and cardiovascular risk.

medicines.uses: Symptomatic relief of allergic rhinitis (sneezing, runny nose, itching) and chronic hives (urticaria).
medicines.commonSideEffects: Headache, fatigue, dry mouth, mild drowsiness (rare).
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Rare severe hypersensitivity reactions (anaphylaxis, rash), palpitations, liver dysfunction.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store between 15°C and 30°C in a dry place.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Can be taken with or without food.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Low clinical risk during pregnancy; consult doctor before use.
medicines.childrenWarning: Tablets for children >6 years (>30kg); use syrup for younger children (2–6 years).
medicines.elderlyWarning: Generally safe; adjust dosage in severe hepatic impairment.

medicines.uses: Treatment of moderate-to-severe fever (viral, post-vaccination) and relief of body aches, toothache, and headache.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Nausea, mild stomach discomfort, rare allergic rash.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Severe hepatotoxicity / liver damage with acute overdose or chronic overuse.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store in a cool, dry place below 30°C.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Take after meals or with water to minimize gastric discomfort.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Generally safe at therapeutic doses when prescribed by a physician.
medicines.childrenWarning: 650mg strength is for adults and adolescents >50kg; not for young children.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Maintain minimum 4–6 hour dosing intervals; do not exceed daily limit.

medicines.uses: Treatment of anaerobic bacterial infections, amebiasis, giardiasis, trichomoniasis, and dental infections.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Metallic taste in mouth, nausea, abdominal cramps, dark urine.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Peripheral neuropathy, encephalopathy, seizures, severe disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store below 30°C in a light-resistant container.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Take during or immediately after meals to reduce stomach irritation.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Contraindicated in first trimester of pregnancy due to organogenesis risk.
medicines.childrenWarning: Pediatric dosage calculated strictly on body weight (mg/kg).
medicines.elderlyWarning: Monitor closely for neurotoxicity due to decreased drug clearance.
medicines.maxDailyDose: 2000mg per 24 hours depending on clinical indication.

medicines.uses: First-line treatment for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus to improve glycemic control.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Diarrhea, nausea, flatulence, stomach cramps, Vitamin B12 deficiency with chronic use.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Lactic acidosis (rare but life-threatening metabolic emergency). Contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store at room temperature (15°C–30°C) away from heat and moisture.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Take during or immediately after meals to lower GI side effects. Swallow XR whole.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Acceptable during pregnancy under specialist endocrinology supervision.
medicines.childrenWarning: Approved for children 10 years and older with Type 2 diabetes.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Regularly monitor renal function (eGFR); contraindicated if eGFR <30 mL/min.
medicines.maxDailyDose: 2550mg per 24 hours for IR (2000mg for XR).

medicines.uses: Relief of mild-to-moderate pain (headache, dysmenorrhea, muscle ache) and fever management.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Rare when used as directed; occasional rash.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Severe hepatotoxicity with acute overdose; severe skin hypersensitivity.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store in a cool, dry place below 30°C.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Can be taken with or after food with water.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Safe at standard therapeutic doses during pregnancy under medical advice.
medicines.childrenWarning: Use pediatric suspension for children under 12 years.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Safe; monitor hepatic function and avoid concomitant alcohol consumption.

medicines.uses: Fast relief from heartburn, acid indigestion, hyperacidity, and gastric discomfort.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Constipation (from calcium), mild laxative effect (from magnesium), belching.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Hypercalcemia, alkalosis, rebound hyperacidity with chronic high-dose use.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store in original package below 25°C in a dry place.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Chew 1–2 tablets after meals or at bedtime, or when symptoms occur.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Safe during pregnancy and lactation if taken as recommended.
medicines.childrenWarning: Not recommended for children under 12 years without medical advice.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Use caution in patients with impaired renal function or hypercalcemia.
medicines.maxDailyDose: Maximum 11 chewable tablets in 24 hours; limit continuous use to 14 days.

medicines.genericName: Famotidine (Zantac 360 formulation; historical Ranitidine withdrawn globally due to NDMA safety concerns)
medicines.uses: Prevention and treatment of heartburn, acid indigestion, and GERD.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Rare CNS effects (confusion in elderly/renal impairment), blood dyscrasias, QT prolongation.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store below 25°C in a dry place protected from light.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Take 15–60 minutes before eating food or drinking beverages that cause heartburn.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and prescribed by physician.
medicines.childrenWarning: Approved for pediatric use under medical supervision with weight-based dosing.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Dose reduction required in moderate-to-severe renal impairment.
medicines.maxDailyDose: 40mg per 24 hours for OTC heartburn relief.

medicines.uses: 24-hour relief of seasonal/perennial allergic rhinitis (sneezing, runny nose) and hives (urticaria).
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Severe allergic reactions (angioedema, anaphylaxis), hepatitis, urinary retention.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Can be taken with or without food.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Use during pregnancy only if potential clinical benefit justifies potential risk to fetus.
medicines.childrenWarning: Use oral solution for children 2–11 years; 10mg tablet for >6 years.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Start at lower dose (5mg) in elderly or renal impairment.

medicines.uses: Treatment of hypertension (high blood pressure) and coronary artery disease.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Edema (swelling of ankles/feet), fatigue, dizziness, flushing.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Severe hypotension, worsening angina, allergic reactions.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store at room temperature protected from light and moisture.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Can be taken with or without food.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
medicines.childrenWarning: Safety and efficacy in children not established.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Start at lower dose in elderly patients.

medicines.uses: Treatment of hypertension, diabetic nephropathy, and reduction of stroke risk.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Dizziness, fatigue, nasal congestion, back pain.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store below 30°C in a dry place.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Can be taken with or without food.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Contraindicated in second and third trimesters of pregnancy.
medicines.childrenWarning: Use with caution in pediatric patients >6 years.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Generally well tolerated; monitor kidney function.

medicines.uses: Treatment of hypothyroidism and thyroid hormone replacement therapy.
medicines.commonSideEffects: Weight loss, tremor, headache, nervousness, palpitations with high dose.
medicines.seriousSideEffects: Cardiac arrhythmias, angina, osteoporosis with chronic overtreatment.
medicines.storageInstructions: Store at room temperature protected from light and moisture.
medicines.beforeAfterFood: Take on an empty stomach with a full glass of water 30-60 minutes before breakfast.
medicines.pregnancyWarning: Safe and essential during pregnancy under strict thyroid monitoring.
medicines.childrenWarning: Dose adjusted strictly by pediatric endocrinologist based on weight/age.
medicines.elderlyWarning: Start with lower doses in elderly or those with cardiac disease.
medicines.maxDailyDose: 300mcg per 24 hours as directed by endocrinologist.

interactions.reason: Increased risk of severe gastrointestinal ulceration/bleeding and reduced cardioprotective effect of Aspirin.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid concurrent use or consult a physician for cardiovascular antiplatelet protection.

interactions.reason: Additive inhibition of cyclooxygenase leading to high risk of gastrointestinal mucosal damage and renal toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination of multiple oral NSAIDs.

interactions.reason: Disulfiram-like reaction causing severe flushing, throbbing headache, nausea, vomiting, and tachycardia.
interactions.recommendation: Strictly avoid alcohol during Flagyl treatment and for at least 48 hours after the last dose.

interactions.reason: Increased risk of liver toxicity due to cumulative depletion of hepatic glutathione.
interactions.recommendation: Limit alcohol consumption while taking Paracetamol.

interactions.reason: Increased risk of liver toxicity due to cumulative depletion of hepatic glutathione.
interactions.recommendation: Limit alcohol consumption while taking Paracetamol.

interactions.reason: Antacids containing divalent cations (calcium/magnesium) can reduce gastrointestinal absorption of oral antibiotics.
interactions.recommendation: Separate doses by at least 2 hours.
